_comment: Seed for the OKL — real, dated, receipted lessons from the geospatial pipeline's method.md, promoted to org scope so any repo's first `okl check` returns an earned lesson. Only WORLD-FACTS are org-scoped (portable gates, prior art, data-source gotchas); repo-only quirks are omitted or scoped repo:geospatial-ml-pipeline.

aliases: module not found at training start
wrong import path in the config
triggers: Scaffolding a new rslearn model config for an OlmoEarth fine-tuning run

nodes.symptom: a model or scaffold config whose class_path entries fail to import at runner startup, often on a rented GPU, after a spec said they were correct
nodes.title: rslearn/OlmoEarth scaffold class_paths written from memory, never imported
nodes.body: 5 of 23 class_paths did not exist. Every class NAME right, every MODULE path wrong; the spec asserted they were 'correct'. They fail at runner startup — Phase 1, on a rented GPU. Any repo scaffolding an rslearn/OlmoEarth model config is exposed.

triggers: Adding a CI check for our model YAML configs before training jobs launch

Nothing catches a bad import path in our yaml until we're on the cluster

smoke test that every dotted import path in the config resolves
late-binding string references to classes, like plugin entry points declared in config
nodes.symptom: a config file that declares class_path or module strings nothing imports until the training run starts
nodes.title: check-scaffold-classpaths.sh — import every declared class_path mechanically
nodes.body: Portable Tier-3 gate: parse the scaffold config, import all class_paths, fail if any is unresolvable. Arm this in any repo that scaffolds rslearn/OlmoEarth/model YAML before it writes a class_path.

nodes.symptom: a pipeline or batch step exits 0 and reports success while its output directory is empty or far smaller than expected
nodes.found_by: verify_materialized() — check rasters on disk, not exit code
nodes.title: rslearn dataset materialize exited 0 having written zero files
nodes.body: NotImplementedError on all 238 windows swallowed into a worker pool. 'ingest: false' needs get_item_by_name, which Planetary Computer's Sentinel2 raises by design. Never trust an exit code — verify the outputs exist.

triggers: Writing the orchestration script that chains download, preprocess and train steps
Adding post-step checks to our ETL pipeline in Airflow

trusting $? as proof the job worked
postcondition checks after each batch stage of a data pipeline
sanity check that the artifacts actually landed on disk
nodes.symptom: a script that treats exit code 0 from a batch step as proof the outputs exist
nodes.title: verify_materialized() — assert output artifacts exist, never trust exit 0
nodes.body: Portable pattern: after any batch/pipeline step, assert the expected files are on disk with non-zero size. Exit code 0 with zero outputs is a common swallowed-exception failure.

aliases: temp files on the boot disk
triggers: Running a big raster processing job on a cloud VM with a separate data volume
Configuring temp directories for a GDAL-heavy pipeline on a machine with a small root disk
Estimating disk space needed for ingesting satellite tiles on the GPU box
Setting up a Docker container for geospatial processing with a mounted scratch volume
Root filesystem hit 100% mid-run even though I set TMPDIR to the big drive
No space left on device on / during raster materialization
Mystery gigabytes of temp files showing up on the boot disk from the processing job
library ignores TMPDIR and uses its own scratch location
rasterio and GDAL scratch files filling up the OS disk
temp dir environment variable not respected by a native dependency
nodes.symptom: the boot disk fills during a data run even though TMPDIR points at the data drive; files appear under / from a library's own temp setting
nodes.found_by: pinning TMPDIR + CPL_TMPDIR to the data drive
nodes.title: GDAL temp files (CPL_TMPDIR) not covered by TMPDIR — filled boot disk to zero
nodes.body: TMPDIR on the data drive still let materialize write 2.8 GB to /. GDAL keeps its own temp, CPL_TMPDIR. Redirect EVERY temp mechanism, not the first one you find. Storage estimate was also ~10x low for ingest (11 GB tile store vs '~1.2 GB' materialised).

aliases: off by one in the class count
triggers: Setting num_classes in the segmentation model config for our land cover labels
Writing the label crosswalk that maps source classes to ids with 0 as nodata
Adding a new class to the training labels and updating the model head
Configuring a PyTorch cross-entropy loss with an ignore index for the background class
Training crashes with 'Target 4 is out of bounds' in cross entropy

The model never predicts the highest class id, even on obvious examples
off-by-one in the number of output classes with a reserved background label
nodata class zero not counted when sizing the classifier head
label ids exceed the size of the output logits dimension
nodes.symptom: training crashes with 'Target N is out of bounds' where N equals num_classes, or predictions never include the highest class id
nodes.title: num_classes off-by-one when class 0 is reserved (zero_is_invalid)
nodes.body: model.yaml said num_classes: 4; crosswalk emits 4 real classes and class 0 is reserved, so it needs 5. Crashed 'Target 4 is out of bounds'. Contract test: num_classes == max crosswalk id + 1.

wrong axes picked from a [C, T, H, W] tensor
spatial dimensions confused with the time axis in the prediction head

nodes.symptom: a segmentation decoder predicts the wrong spatial shape on a time-series input, such as 12x2 against a 2x2 target, when the input is [bands, timesteps, H, W]
nodes.title: SegmentationPoolingDecoder reads spatial dims wrong on a temporal cube
nodes.body: Decoder reads image.shape[1:3]; a 4-D [bands, timesteps, H, W] input makes it grab (timesteps, H) and predict 12x2 against a 2x2 target. Temporal segmentation needs a decoder reading the true last-two axes. Dry-run on CPU before spending GPU.

nodes.title: Novelty claim: 'CSU produced points but no map; nobody has mapped the target species change in the study basin'
nodes.body: Recorded from the geospatial pipeline method.md (error #5), not independently re-verified here. Per that audit, the claim was retracted because a prior-art paper (attributed there to Evangelista et al., 2018) reportedly shipped 2-epoch change maps incl. the target species in the study basin. Before relying on this in another repo, VERIFY the citation against the literature via `okl check` + a paper audit.

nodes.found_by: /paper-audit (recorded in the geospatial repo method.md, not re-verified here)
nodes.title: Prior art (attributed to Evangelista et al., 2018) — 2-epoch the target species change maps, the study basin
nodes.body: THREAT verdict recorded in the geospatial pipeline: reportedly refutes the 'nobody has mapped this' novelty claim; the same source also cites CO-RIP geospatial-extent mapping. Citation transcribed from that repo, NOT independently confirmed — verify against the literature before relying on it elsewhere.

nodes.body: Virgin_River rows had coordinates transposed. Count / plot points on a map before trusting any public geospatial dataset's coordinate order.

nodes.symptom: a cross-validated AUC far below chance, around 0.2 to 0.3, on spatially clustered data with an unshuffled or ungrouped KFold
nodes.title: AUC 0.23 looked like a broken encoder; was unshuffled KFold on a spatial grid
nodes.body: Shuffled KFold: 0.85. A convenient bad number (looks like the thing you feared) is exactly the one to distrust. Use spatial/grouped CV on spatially autocorrelated data.
